texts: My husband has been posted abroad for eight months and I still set out two cups of tea every morning before remembering.
sleepless, bereft, apart
Since he left for the other city my nights have become endless and I lie awake staring at the ceiling, hollow and sleepless. Please write a doha about the ache of being apart from the one I long for.
need a doha about being away from the person you love, cant sleep, feel empty
Without you the nights have no end and the days no meaning; the beloved is far and the heart is hollow.
chakor, fish, parted
I am the chakor bird staring at a far-off sky that never brings my love near, and the fish flopping on dry ground for water: write me a doha on the pain of being kept apart from the Beloved.
doha with a chakor bird and a fish out of water, aching for the Beloved
The chakor gazes all night at the empty sky, the fish on dry land gasps for water; so I live without you.
My friend sits by her window each night like the chakor bird, and her face looks like a fish out of water since her fiance moved away.
grindstone, bell, absence
Ever since my wife went back to her village the grindstone sits unused and I can hear the bell from the neighbor's puja all night.
The grindstone is still and the bell rings hollow; without the Beloved even sound has become silence.
a doha with grindstone and bell about missing someone so much it hurts

My mother's old grindstone still sits silent in the corner and the bell on the shelf rings hollow, because the beloved is gone and every familiar sound reminds me of the one who is no longer here with me.
My soul is a bird in a cage and my beloved is across the water on the other shore. Compose a doha on this separation, with a small boat I can see but cannot board, tormenting me day and night.
doha pls, caged heart, boat leaving without me, missing my beloved so much
The caged bird looks at the far shore, the boat sails without me; the Beloved lives and I am bereft.
I feel like I live inside a cage since she left; every evening I watch the fishermen's boat go out and wish I were on it.
cage, boat, far shore
lamp, empty night
The lamp burns down in the empty hours, the night is long, and my beloved is still not here.
I keep a lamp lit by the window every night since he left for the army, though the ceiling lights work just fine.
doha about leaving a lamp lit for someone who is far away and missing
Every evening I light a lamp at the window for the one who has not come back, and I sit sleepless as it dies out, so please write a doha about this endless waiting in the dark.
At the cremation ground the water pot is cracked and the beloved is gone; what is left of the world is smoke.
We carried a pot of water to the cremation ground for my sister's husband, and she has not slept a full night since he went.
At the cremation ground I stood with my pot of water and wept, for the one I yearned for had left me forever; compose a doha about the kind of absence that empties the whole world.
doha: lover gone forever, cremation ground and a pot of water
cremation ground, pot of water
The palanquin went and my shadow stayed, a thin companion on a road that carries nothing now.
After the palanquin took my sister away to her in-laws, my own shadow in the lane looked suddenly lonely and I missed her badly.

In the afternoon heat I only see my own shadow walking beside me where the palanquin once carried my bride, and a longing deeper than words grips me. Please write a doha about the empty road without her.
doha with a palanquin leaving and a shadow staying behind, missing someone
shadow, empty palanquin
A thief came in the night and took my beloved with him, and left me my breath only to feel the loss.
doha like a thief took my peace when my partner left, im not okay
Since he left I have eaten nothing and slept less, as if some thief robbed me of everything except the pain of it.
There was a thief in the night who stole my sleep, my appetite, and my reason when my beloved walked out, and I have been bereft since. Compose a doha about this theft of everything by absence.
thief of sleep
The diamond on her finger glitters in an empty room, and I am left holding a ring as cold as the distance between us. Please write a doha about longing for the Beloved, long and gentle.
doha about a diamond ring left behind and the heart missing its owner
diamond in an empty room
The diamond keeps its brilliance, I keep my ache; what good is a jewel when the one who gave it is far?
My fiancee left her diamond ring on the shelf before she traveled and now I sit staring at it every night.
The rooms feel like a stranger's since my daughter left for hostel, and I keep setting her plate out at dinner.
a doha for when your beloved is far away and the evenings feel so long and silent
Sleepless I count the hours of an endless night, for the beloved is far and the heart has lost its voice.
parted, sleepless
When my mother left for the long pilgrimage the whole place fell silent, the evenings stretched out and I forgot how to sleep. Write me a doha for a heart parted from the one it needs.
Honestly I stopped wearing my gold chain after my husband left for the Gulf, it just felt wrong without him to show it to.
The gold fades on the wrist of the waiting one, for her true ornament is the beloved who is far away.

My gold bracelets have lost their shine since the day my husband went across the border; no ornament consoles a woman who waits and no festival can lift her heavy, longing heart, so write something for me.
doha pls: gold jewelry means nothing now that my beloved is away
gold without the beloved
Everyone around me laughs at the wedding and dances, but I sit alone in a corner like a ghost, hungry and sleepless, for the one I yearn for is not here to see it.
I attended my best friend's wedding and felt like a ghost because the person I wanted beside me hadn't come back from his tour yet.
bereft among the crowd
a doha about being among people yet feeling empty because the one you love isnt there
The festival goes on, the songs rise, and I sit apart, for the Beloved is missing from the circle.
When the full moon rises over the empty courtyard I cannot bear it, because we used to sit and watch it together, and now it only mocks my sleepless, bereft nights. Please write me a doha.
doha about the moon rising and the one i miss being far away
the moon without you
Last full moon night I called him just to say look at the moon, and he was too far to see it with me.
The moon rises over an empty courtyard and mocks the one who sits without her beloved.
loom and absence
The shuttle moves across the loom but the heart's weave is cut; she weaves and waits for the one who left.

At her loom my mother weaves slowly now, her hands trembling and her eyes elsewhere, because her husband is far away and no cloth is warm enough for the cold nights without him. Please compose a doha.
doha with a loom, a woman waiting for her beloved to come back
My grandmother used to sit at the loom for hours after Grandpa left for work in another city, never weaving a straight line.
The rains have come and gone, the beloved has not; my hours are cold and no one is beside me.
a doha for waiting for someone who said theyd be back and isnt
he did not return
He promised to be back before the rains and now the first showers are here, and I just sit by the window and wait.

The monsoon came and the whole village sang, but I could only stare at the road, sleepless and aching, because the one who promised to return before the rains has still not appeared. Write a doha for me.
spinning wheel, cremation ground
doha about a spinning wheel left still, a cremation ground, the beloved gone
After the cremation my father keeps touching my late mother's spinning wheel and then goes silent for hours.
The spinning wheel is idle, the cremation ground is quiet; the one who spun my life has gone beyond.
I came to the cremation ground to scatter her remains and the spinning wheel in our old room still stands still; I ache so deeply I cannot sleep. Compose a doha about this heart-rending absence.
palace and a fallen leaf
We toured the palace on our honeymoon, and walking there alone this year I picked up a fallen leaf and wept quietly.
doha: an empty palace and a single leaf, missing someone deeply
The palace stands and the leaf falls; what use are halls and gardens when the Beloved is not within them?

The great palace is empty without him, and a single fallen leaf drifts across the courtyard, a small sign of everything that has withered since he left; write me a doha that captures the stillness of his absence.
ache without end
The Beloved is far; I am an unlit, silent place, and sleep has gone to keep him company.
a doha about longing so intense you cant sleep, because the one you love is far
Since my partner moved to another country the quiet in our rooms is so loud that I can barely stay in them, and the evenings are the hardest of all, so please write me a doha.
My wife went to her mother's last week and the bed feels huge and cold, I keep reaching across it.
Every evening I fill a pot of water and light the lamp the way my wife did, hoping that her chores will somehow bring her back.
Pot of water and lit lamp, the bed is made; only the Beloved is absent, and he is everything.
doha about someone doing the daily rituals of their absent partner, lamp and pot of water
lamp, pot of water, waiting
I fill the pot of water at the village pond just as she used to, and light a lamp by the bed, but the one I wait for does not come; write a doha for a heart long left behind.
doha with an arrow and a spinning wheel, aching for someone far away
An arrow of pain pierced my chest the day she walked away, and at the spinning wheel, mending nothing, I sit and think that even yarn is easier to hold on to than her memory. Write a doha for me.
Her leaving hit me like an arrow, and now I keep cranking my grandmother's old spinning wheel just to hear a noise at night.
The arrow of parting struck deep, the spinning wheel turns and the yarn breaks; without the Beloved, nothing holds.
arrow and spinning wheel
cracked pot of water
After he left, the pot of water cracked in the heat and I felt it was a sign, like my life had a hole that nothing could fill.
doha about a cracked pot of water as my heart without the one I miss
My pot of water sits cracked on the shelf the way my heart cracked the day my beloved left and never returned; I wonder if anyone can fill the emptiness that came after. Please write a doha for me.
The pot of water has cracked and the beloved is far; whatever I pour in drains out as longing.
I stand at the crossroads every evening, hoping the road will bring him back, though the dust settles and no one comes, and my sleepless nights carry on. Write a doha for this long, hopeless waiting.
Every evening after work my mother walks to the crossroads at the end of our lane, hoping my brother's bus will bring him back from the city.
doha about waiting at a crossroads for the one who left, missing him so much
At the crossroads I gaze in every direction, and every road returns with dust but never with the Beloved.
crossroads, no beloved
The moth wheels about the light that will undo him, and I about a memory that will not return to me.
moth and longing
She keeps going back to his old messages like a moth to a glow, though they only make the distance more painful.
doha with a moth circling a light, longing for someone who's far away, aching

The moth circles a light and cannot reach what it craves; I too circle the memory of my beloved, never touching, never forgetting, never sleeping. Please write a doha on parted hearts with a moth in it.
just need a doha on this ache of him being gone
Seven springs have come and gone since my husband passed on, and I still wake at night and reach for his side of the bed.
I don't know how to explain it, but since my husband died in the spring the whole world seems to have gone gray and quiet, and I wake each night expecting his breath beside me. Write a doha for it.
an empty place
Gray is the dawn and gray the evening; the Beloved has crossed beyond and left me alone.
There's a rusty lock on the gate he promised to fix before he left, and a bee keeps buzzing there, and I keep waiting.
bee, locked gate
a doha about a locked gate and a bee, waiting for the one who went away
The bee hums by the locked gate, the key went with the beloved; the garden withers waiting.
A bee hums at the lock on the garden gate, the key lost somewhere on the road my husband took, and I stand and wonder when the Beloved will return to open the gate again, so write me a doha.
The physician says there's nothing wrong with me, but since she left I haven't eaten and I can't stop staring at the river.
physician, river, parted
The physician reads my pulse and finds no fever; he cannot know that the sickness is a river between us.
The physician came and felt my pulse by the river bank, and found nothing wrong, but I told him that the only medicine is the Beloved who has gone; write me a doha for this unspoken illness.
doha: a physician cant cure me, i need the person who went across the river
We were together for ten years and honestly I didn't realize her touchstone worth until she took the job abroad and the rooms went quiet.
As the touchstone tells the metal, so parting tells the heart how deep the Beloved was set.
The touchstone shows the worth of a metal and so does separation show the worth of the one we love, so write me a doha which says that only distance proves how dear the Beloved was to this heart.
the touchstone of parting
doha about how you only learn the worth of someone when they are far away, touchstone maybe
The lotus closes at dusk and the loom lies idle; what is a day to one who has lost her Beloved?
doha with a lotus and a loom, missing my partner badly
On the lotus pond the evening is still and the loom stands idle, because the one who wove my days is gone, and I have forgotten how to sleep or even to sit. Please write a doha for me.
I used to sit by the lotus pond with him at dusk, and now I go alone and carry his old loom shawl.
lotus, idle loom
Sitting beneath the neem I watched the shadow of a crow circle the courtyard where my beloved last stood, and I thought: even the crow has a nest, and I have only this endless empty waiting.
crow and shadow
doha about a crow and its shadow on the wall that might bring news of a far-away beloved
A crow keeps sitting on our wall, casting a long shadow, since my son left for the city, and my mother says it is bringing news.
The crow calls and its shadow circles; if you bring word of the Beloved, I will give you my eyes.
The lotus lives for the light, and I for the one who left; without them both of us wilt.
My sister's face has faded like a lotus in the drought since her fiance left and she barely eats anything now.
The lotus in the pond lifts toward the sky while I sit sleepless on the bank, bereft and wasting away, for the one I loved is gone and no flower can console me. Please write me a doha.
a wilting lotus
short doha about a lotus wilting, like someone missing their beloved
From the temple steps I watch the palanquin vanish down the road with my beloved inside it, and I stand there long after the dust settles, weeping for all that is gone. Please compose a doha for me.
doha with a temple and a palanquin, the ache of someone leaving
The palanquin has turned the bend and the temple is empty; I am a small speck of sorrow on the steps.
We stood outside the temple while my sister's palanquin left for her husband's village, and I could not stop shaking afterwards.
temple, palanquin, farewell
It's been four months since he left and I still can't sleep before three, I just keep wondering if he misses me too.
The night is long, my hours are long, and they do not end, for the Beloved is not here to cut them.
Late every night I lie on the roof and count the hours, wondering whether she is thinking of me too, and the days pass in hunger and sleeplessness, because without her nothing tastes of anything.
nights too long
doha about nights that go on forever when your partner is far
distant beloved, sleepless
doha: i miss her so bad i cant function

I watched everyone's families reunite at the festival of lights while my own beloved remained thousands of miles away, and I sat in a dark corner feeling the hollowness in my chest swell, so please write me a doha.
My phone lights up when anyone texts and every time I hope it's her, and every time it is not.
Yearning for the one who is gone, I forget how to eat, how to sleep, how to speak.
Sandalwood cannot cool and diamonds cannot warm the one whose beloved is far; only his return can heal.
sandalwood, diamond, ache
Though the sandalwood paste cools my brow it cannot cool the ache; though the diamond shines at my throat I cannot be consoled, because it is only the sight of my beloved that I need.
a doha with sandalwood and a diamond, longing that nothing can soothe
My mother rubs sandalwood paste on her brow every night when the missing him gets too bad, and my father's diamond ring lies on her pillow.
The rainbird cries for the rain and the thief steals the night; I too am bereft of my beloved.
rainbird and thief
A thief broke into our village shop the night my husband left and the rainbird kept calling, but I'd already lost everything that mattered.
The rainbird cries for the rain and I cry for the beloved; and the thief of night steals my sleep; compose a doha of a heart parted from the one it needs most.
doha with a rainbird crying for rain and a thief at night, a heart missing the beloved

At the riverside temple I lit a small light each evening, begging the river to carry my message to my distant beloved, and when she doesn't come I am tormented all night by the silence; please write a doha.
The river carries my message to the temple of the far shore, and my beloved does not read the writing of the water.
temple, river, message
doha: sending a message down the river past the temple to my far-off beloved
I send a small note floating down the river by the temple every full night for him, even though I know it is silly.
honestly cant stop thinking about her, give me a doha about being apart
The nights are long for those who are parted, and the dawn only brings the same absence.
My husband works on a ship, and I count the months on a calendar on the kitchen wall, and some days I just cry into the dal.
bereft, wakeful, apart
ugh i miss him so much, can you write me a doha about being away from the one you love, sleepless and hollow, and doing nothing but staring at the phone all day
The mountain stands unmoved, the cremation ground is quiet, and the widow's heart is a cold hearth.
mountain, cremation ground, waiting
Beneath the great mountain, near the cremation ground, a woman sits and waits for the husband who never came back from the war; write me a doha that echoes the vast silence of a life left behind.
My grandmother still looks toward the mountain each dusk where my grandfather's body was carried to the cremation ground, and says nothing.
doha about mountain and cremation ground, missing the departed with empty hands
moon, tilak, absence
doha with the moon and a tilak on the forehead, aching for a far beloved
The moon is thin and the tilak has dried; who will mark my forehead now that the beloved is gone?
Every night I look at the moon and touch my tilak, and I realise he hasn't called in six days.
When the moon wanes I touch the tilak on my forehead and remember his hand putting it there, and now I am left with a faded mark and a sleepless night. Write a doha for me.
Like a traveler without a destination I walk each day, and the swan drifting on the lake reminds me of the one who left me; write me a doha for a heart long parted from the one it needs.
traveler, swan, parted
I saw a lone swan on the lake this morning, and it reminded me of my brother, who left as a traveler and hasn't written in months.
doha about a traveler and a swan, ache for someone far away
The swan floats on, the traveler walks on, and I sit between them knowing no place has my Beloved in it.
Our parrot still says my husband's name every morning, and my eyes sting like they are rubbed with salt.
doha: parrot calling the name of the one who left, salt of sorrow
The parrot repeats the name of the departed, and salt stands on every cheek that heard it.
parrot, salt of parting
The parrot in our courtyard repeats her name in my voice, and I taste the salt of my own sorrow in it; please write a doha about the emptiness left by someone who is far from me.
After my beloved left for the war there was no one to talk to, and the dawn found me awake again, my body thin and my heart as heavy as lead, so please compose a doha for me about this.
doha about getting thin and sleepless from missing a far-off lover
waiting thin
My roommate hasn't slept properly since her boyfriend moved overseas and she looks like a ghost of herself these days.
The heart grows thin and faint, for the one who gave it radiance is far away.
my tongue goes numb when i say her name, doha about missing someone
My tongue is silent and the heart speaks; the Beloved is far, and the whole body has become a name.
tongue-tied by absence
When I tried to tell my mother I missed him my tongue froze, and she just held me until I could cry.
how my tongue clings to the roof of my mouth when I try to say his name, mute with sorrow; please write me a doha so true that it could be spoken by someone whose beloved has gone far away.
My grandmother sorts rice with a winnowing fan and mutters my grandfather's name without noticing it, her tongue forty years faithful.
When the winnowing fan lifts the grain from the chaff, my aching tongue still has only his name to repeat, the single grain left in the chaff of an empty life. Write a doha for the parted heart.
The winnowing fan sifts the husk from the grain, and absence sifts my days until only his name remains on my tongue.
winnowing fan, tongue, his name
doha with a winnowing fan and a tongue that only says one name
The cuckoo sings and the churn turns, but the butter will not come when the beloved is far.
The cuckoo sings in the mango grove, but her song only wounds me because my beloved is not here to hear it, and the churn turns without butter; write a doha about the heartbreak of parting.
cuckoo, churn, apart
The cuckoo calls every morning in our garden, and my mother churns buttermilk with a face so tired because my father left the village.
doha with a cuckoo and a churn, missing the beloved who is far away
I have forgotten how it feels to sleep through a night since you left, my heart goes round and round with the memory of your voice, and it is unbearable; please write a doha for me, I beg you.
doha for when the person you love is in a different timezone and you miss them
After he got the transfer I stopped sleeping properly, I wake at 4 am and check my phone for his goodnight text from another timezone.
since you left
Without you the night becomes a wasteland, the heart a wanderer, and sleep a stranger I have forgotten how to welcome.

The potter's wheel spins without my hands on the clay now that my beloved is gone, and the pot I started remains unfinished at the edge of the village. Please compose a doha for this deep, wordless loneliness.
My uncle the potter hasn't touched his clay since his wife passed, and the half-made pots are cracking in the yard.
The potter's hands lie idle, the clay dries unformed, and the Beloved who gave the shape has gone.
potter's clay, unfinished
doha with a potter and clay left unfinished, grief of missing someone dear
skeleton of waiting
I am a skeleton of my own self, wasted by waiting; only the Beloved's glance can put flesh upon my bones.
On this empty night I feel stripped to the bone by the long absence of the one I love, nothing but a skeleton of myself, so write me a doha of such stark sorrow, spare and quiet and bare.
After he left she faded so much that people say she looks like a skeleton, and she says she is only waiting for him.
doha about becoming a skeleton from longing for the beloved
Up in the forest the bitter gourd vines have withered, and my life tastes as bitter, with nobody to cook for and nobody to wait on, now that my beloved has left; please write me a doha.
My wife used to cook bitter gourd for me every Sunday, and now I walk past the vegetable cart at the forest edge and can't buy any.
doha with a bitter gourd and a forest, aching for the beloved
bitter gourd, forest, bereft
The forest is green and the bitter gourd bitter, and all of life tastes of the Beloved's absence.
The lotus waits upon the water; oh my Beloved, when will you return to this lake?
Our lotus pond is empty now that my father is gone, and Mother goes there every evening and just stands.
lotus, empty lake
doha about a lotus on a lake missing the one who has gone
The lotus floats alone upon the lake and the water is still, and in the silence of the rain I miss you more than all the poets could ever say. Please write a doha for me.
